title: Dedicated SLA Spectra: customer profile & scaling simulator
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a lightweight interactive 'SLA Spectra' that lets sales/solutions and PMs model a customer's dedicated capacity request across three axes: latency SLO, reserved throughput (tokens/sec & concurrency), and GPU class. The simulator should output recommended GPU family, minimum reserved capacity, suggested autoscale policy (burst allowance, cooldown), and a communication-ready SLA summary. Purpose: speed up intake, reduce back-and-forth for enterprise customers, and produce deterministic recommendations for Dedicated onboarding conversations.
context: We receive lengthy email/Forms intake that often lacks lateral signals (sequence length distribution, concurrent sessions, tail-latency tolerance). That causes repeated sizing calls and over-provisioning. Existing capacity playbooks are numerous but spread across docs and tribal knowledge. Sales and Solutions need a repeatable fast estimation tool that ties to our contractual SLA bands and supported GPU classes.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive simulator UI (internal console widget / Google Sheets v0) that accepts: peak qps, median tokens per request, 95th percentile latency target, percent of requests requiring deterministic output (SLA sensitivity), and typical concurrency pattern (steady vs bursty).

Simulator returns: recommended GPU class (e.g., A100-80/RTX8000/4090-equivalent), baseline reserved throughput (tokens/s), concurrency limits, suggested burst credit and cooldown, and a short SLA blurb (<= 300 chars) for first-touch email.
Recommendations map to existing Dedicated SKU tiers and include cost ballpark and fallback options (lower-cost quantized models, routing to best-effort pool).
Exportable artifact (PDF or shareable Drive link) summarizing inputs, outputs, and reasoning.
Simulator guidance validated by two recent enterprise engagements (post-launch pilot), and at least one engineering sign-off that recommendations are implementable.
tasks: Workshop with Sales & Solutions to catalog common intake patterns (Feb 26)
Draft initial sizing heuristics and mapping table from throughput & latency to GPU family (PM + Applied ML)
Prototype spreadsheet simulator with formulas and conditional mapping (v0)
Build internal console widget spec for V1 (UI/UX + copy)
Run 3 pilot customers through simulator and collect feedback
Incorporate engineering constraints: minimum batch sizes, KV cache hit assumptions, and quantization options
Finalize mapping to SKU & reserved commit profiles and publish internal doc
notes: Heuristics should be conservative by default but expose knobs for aggressive cost optimization.

Important signals to capture: request token distribution (P50/P95), session stickiness (how often same session continues), acceptable failover (route to best-effort vs degrade quality), and legal constraints (data residency).
Consider exposing a 'confidence score' based on input completeness; low-confidence results route to Solutions for manual sizing call.
We should link the simulator outputs to contract templates so SLA language is consistent with legal-approved tiers.
